title: Transformations of graphs
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point covers dilations, reflections and translations together as one overview, but each bank point teaches only one transformation type, and the Year 12 combining-transformations point goes beyond this Year 11 depth, so no single bank point is the same idea.

draft.title: Transformations of graphs
card: y = f(x − h) + k moves the graph h units right and k units up. A minus inside the bracket moves the graph right.
y = −f(x) reflects the graph in the x-axis. y = f(−x) reflects it in the y-axis.
y = a f(x) stretches the graph by a factor of a from the x-axis. y = f(x/b) stretches it by a factor of b from the y-axis.
Each point (x, y) moves in a set way. For example, y = (x + 1)² − 4 is y = x² moved 1 left and 4 down, so its vertex is (−1, −4).
draft.remember: Outside the bracket changes y. Inside the bracket changes x, and in the opposite way to how it looks.

a.q: The graph of y = x² is translated 3 units right and 2 units down. What is the new rule?
a.why: Moving right by 3 means x is replaced by (x − 3), and moving down by 2 means subtracting 2. The option with (x + 3) moves the graph left, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Right 3 puts a minus inside the bracket.

b.q: The point (6, 4) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = −f(x/2)?
b.why: Replacing x with x/2 stretches the graph by a factor of 2 from the y-axis, so x goes from 6 to 12. The negative sign outside reflects in the x-axis, so y goes from 4 to −4. (3, −4) is tempting, but it halves x instead of doubling it.
b.clue: Deal with x and y separately: one is stretched, one is flipped.
